judgments.justification: “higher average event-F1 (78.4%) than Lanyard-TS (77.2%) across the five benchmarks” reports the descriptive 1.2-point advantage.
It reports “higher event-F1 on four benchmarks” with the correct names and “equal event-F1 on Quayside-Grid v2.”
The passage does not mention the absence of statistical tests or limit its conclusion to descriptive evidence.
It discusses Dunmore-Iso runtime but does not report Sprocket-AD’s event-F1 advantage over Dunmore-Iso.
“lower median detection delay…on three benchmarks” and “higher delay on two” correctly identifies all datasets and directions.
“the full model…outperforms variants” reports all ablations, including the decline from 78.4% to 75.8% without both components.
No input-window sensitivity results are reported.
“more parameter-efficient…faster in training…and inference…than Lanyard-TS” reports the correct metrics, directions, and values.
It reports the Quayside tie but not the revised labels, version incomparability, or caution.
“higher average event-F1…across the five benchmarks, with higher event-F1 on four benchmarks” directly reports the required advantage.
“equal event-F1 on Quayside-Grid v2 (78.4 vs 78.4)” shows that Sprocket-AD’s advantage was not uniform.
